note: Mastering English Library dictionary. Definitions, examples and Arabic by Mastering English Library. Levels: CEFR-J Wordlist (Tono Lab, TUFS) and Octanove Vocabulary Profile (CC BY-SA 4.0). IPA: ipa-dict (MIT).

senses.def: money that is paid regularly to a worker, usually weekly or hourly
ex: The minimum wage went up last year.
He earns a low wage.

senses.def: a strong vehicle with four wheels pulled by horses or used to carry goods
ex: The farmer loaded hay onto the wagon.
The settlers travelled west in wagons.

senses.def: the narrow part in the middle of the body, above the hips
ex: She wore a belt round her waist.
The water came up to my waist.

senses.def: to stay in a place or delay doing something until something happens or someone arrives
ex: Please wait here for a moment.
I'm waiting for the bus.

senses.def: a period of time spent waiting
ex: We had a long wait at the airport.

mistake.wrong: I am waiting him at the station.
mistake.right: I am waiting for him at the station.
mistake.note: Wait needs 'for' before the person or thing you are waiting for; Arabic انتظر takes a direct object.

senses.def: a journey on foot for pleasure or exercise
ex: Let's go for a walk in the park.
It's a ten-minute walk to the station.

senses.def: to move along on foot at a normal speed
ex: I walk to school every day.
She walked the dog before breakfast.

senses.def: a person who walks, especially for pleasure
ex: The path is popular with walkers.
He is a keen walker.

senses.def: the activity of going places on foot for exercise or pleasure
ex: Walking is good for your health.
We went walking in the hills.

senses.def: a small flat case for carrying paper money and cards
ex: I left my wallet at home.
He took some notes out of his wallet.

senses.def: to lie and roll about in mud or water for pleasure
ex: The pigs wallowed in the mud.

senses.def: to spend too much time enjoying an unpleasant feeling
ex: Stop wallowing in self-pity and do something.

senses.def: a nut with a hard round shell that grows on a tree
ex: She added chopped walnuts to the cake.
The table is made of walnut.

senses.def: to become weaker or smaller over time
ex: Public interest in the story began to wane.
His enthusiasm waned after a few weeks.

senses.def: to wish to have or do something
ex: I want a glass of water.
She wants to learn French.

senses.def: a lack of something
ex: Many people suffer from want of food.

mistake.wrong: I want that you come with me.
mistake.right: I want you to come with me.
mistake.note: After want, use object + to-infinitive, not 'that'.

senses.def: a period of fighting between countries or groups
ex: The war lasted for six years.
The two countries are at war.

senses.def: a room in a hospital with beds for patients
ex: She works in the children's ward.
The nurse walked round the ward.

senses.def: one of the areas a town is divided into for voting
ex: He represents the ward on the local council.

senses.def: a tall cupboard for hanging clothes
ex: She hung the dress in the wardrobe.

senses.def: all the clothes that a person owns
ex: I need a new winter wardrobe.

senses.def: the quality of being slightly hot
ex: We sat near the fire for its warmth.
The warmth of the sun made me sleepy.

senses.def: friendly feelings towards other people
ex: She greeted us with great warmth.

senses.def: to tell someone about a possible danger or problem so that they can avoid it
ex: The sign warns drivers of ice on the road.
I warned him not to touch the wire.

mistake.wrong: She warned me for the dog.
mistake.right: She warned me about the dog.
mistake.note: Use warn someone about/of a danger, not 'for'.

senses.def: a statement or sign that tells you about a possible danger or problem
ex: The storm came without warning.
The label has a health warning.

senses.def: a soldier or fighter, especially in the past
ex: The warriors rode into battle on horses.
He was a brave warrior.

senses.def: careful because you think something may be dangerous or cause problems
ex: Be wary of strangers who ask for money.
She gave him a wary look.

senses.def: the past form of 'am' and 'is'
ex: I was tired after the journey.
The film was very funny.

senses.def: used with an -ing form or a past participle in past tenses
ex: She was reading when I called.
The window was broken by the wind.

mistake.wrong: Yesterday I am at home.
mistake.right: Yesterday I was at home.
mistake.note: Use was or were for the past of be; do not leave the verb in the present.

senses.def: a flying insect with a yellow and black body that can sting
ex: A wasp stung me on the arm.
Wasps built a nest under the roof.

senses.def: no longer needed and thrown away
ex: Waste paper is collected every week.
Waste water is cleaned before it goes into the river.

senses.def: the use of more of something than you need, or use that gives no benefit
ex: It's a waste of money to buy two.
Don't go – it's a waste of time.

senses.def: things that are thrown away because they are no longer wanted
ex: Factories must not dump waste in the river.

senses.def: to use more of something than is needed, or use it without good result
ex: Don't waste water.
We wasted an hour waiting in the queue.

senses.def: a small clock that you wear on your wrist
ex: My watch is five minutes slow.
He looked at his watch.

senses.def: to look at something for a period of time, especially something that moves or changes
ex: We watched a film last night.
She watched the children play.

senses.def: to be careful about something
ex: Watch out for the broken step.

mistake.wrong: I saw TV last night.
mistake.right: I watched TV last night.
mistake.note: Use watch (not see) for TV and activities with movement; Arabic شاهد/رأى both become 'see' by mistake.

senses.def: the clear liquid that falls as rain and fills rivers and seas
ex: Can I have a glass of water?
The water in the lake is very clean.

senses.def: to pour water on plants or soil
ex: She waters the flowers every morning.
Don't forget to water the garden.

senses.def: the part of a town beside the sea, a river or a lake
ex: We had dinner at a restaurant on the waterfront.
The waterfront was full of people.

senses.def: a raised line of water moving across the surface of the sea
ex: The children jumped over the waves.
Big waves crashed onto the rocks.

senses.def: a movement of the hand to say hello or goodbye
ex: She gave us a wave from the window.

senses.def: to move your hand from side to side as a greeting or signal
ex: He waved goodbye to his friends.
The crowd waved flags.

senses.def: a soft substance that melts easily, used for making candles and polish
ex: The candle wax dripped onto the table.
Bees make wax for their honeycombs.

senses.def: to cover or polish something with wax
ex: He waxed the floor until it shone.

senses.def: a method or manner of doing something
ex: What is the best way to learn English?
I like the way she sings.

senses.def: the path or direction you take to go somewhere
ex: Can you tell me the way to the station?
I'm on my way home.

mistake.wrong: I like the way of cooking this dish.
mistake.right: I like the way this dish is cooked.
mistake.note: Say 'the way + clause', not 'the way of' + -ing, when you mean how something is done.

senses.def: difficult to control because of doing unexpected or selfish things
ex: The wayward teenager ignored all advice.
A wayward child ran off down the street.

senses.def: used by a speaker to talk about themselves and one or more other people
ex: We live in Riyadh.
We are going to the beach.

senses.def: not physically strong
ex: She felt weak after the illness.
The bridge is too weak for heavy lorries.

senses.def: not good at something, or not good enough
ex: My maths is weak.
He gave a weak excuse.

senses.def: to become weaker or to make something weaker
ex: The illness weakened her heart.
The currency has weakened this year.

senses.def: in a way that lacks strength or energy
ex: He smiled weakly from his hospital bed.
She nodded weakly.

senses.def: the state of not being strong
ex: He felt weakness in his legs after the flu.

senses.def: a fault or lack of skill in someone or something
ex: Shyness is her main weakness.
Everyone has strengths and weaknesses.

senses.def: having a lot of money or valuable things
ex: She comes from a wealthy family.
A wealthy businessman built the hospital.

senses.def: an object, such as a gun or knife, used to hurt or kill people
ex: The police found a weapon in the car.
Some countries have nuclear weapons.

senses.def: very tired, especially after a long time doing something
ex: The weary travellers stopped to rest.
She gave a weary smile.

senses.def: no longer interested in something because it has gone on too long
ex: I'm weary of all this arguing.

senses.def: the way in which threads are woven together, or the pattern they make
ex: The cloth has a tight weave.
The basket has an unusual weave.

senses.def: to marry (formal or literary)
ex: The couple wed in a small ceremony.
She wed him last spring.

senses.def: a ceremony in which two people get married
ex: We are going to my cousin's wedding.
The wedding was held in a garden.

senses.def: a wild plant growing where it is not wanted
ex: The garden was full of weeds.
He pulled up the weeds by hand.

senses.def: a period of seven days
ex: I go swimming twice a week.
See you next week.

senses.def: how heavy someone or something is
ex: He is trying to lose weight.
What is the weight of this box?

senses.def: a heavy object used in exercise
ex: He lifts weights at the gym.

senses.def: very strange and unusual, often in a way that is hard to explain
ex: I had a weird dream last night.
It's weird that nobody called.

senses.def: used to greet someone who has arrived
ex: Welcome to our home!
Welcome back!

senses.def: to greet someone who arrives in a friendly way
ex: The hotel manager welcomed the guests.
They welcomed us with tea.

senses.def: to be pleased about something
ex: We welcome your comments.

senses.def: received with pleasure; wanted
ex: You are always welcome here.
A cup of tea would be very welcome.

senses.def: a greeting or the way you receive someone
ex: They gave us a warm welcome.

mistake.wrong: Welcome in Dubai!
mistake.right: Welcome to Dubai!
mistake.note: Use 'welcome to' a place, not 'in'.

senses.def: the health, happiness and safety of a person or group
ex: The teacher cares about the welfare of her students.
Animal welfare is important.

senses.def: money and other help given by the government to people in need
ex: He lived on welfare for a year.

senses.def: in good health
ex: I don't feel well today.
You look well!

senses.def: in a good or successful way
ex: She speaks English very well.
The meeting went well.

senses.def: completely or carefully
ex: Mix the eggs well before you add the flour.

mistake.wrong: He speaks English good.
mistake.right: He speaks English well.
mistake.note: Use the adverb well (not the adjective good) to describe how someone does something.

senses.def: the past form of 'are', and of 'be' with you, we and they
ex: We were at home all evening.
They were very tired after the trip.

senses.def: used in imagined situations instead of 'was'
ex: If I were you, I would stay at home.

senses.def: in or towards the direction where the sun goes down
ex: The west coast is rainy.
We live on the west side of town.

senses.def: towards the west
ex: The road goes west for ten miles.

senses.def: the direction where the sun goes down
ex: The sun sets in the west.
The village lies to the west of the river.

senses.def: in or from the west of a place
ex: She lives in western France.
The wind blew from the western hills.

senses.def: relating to Europe and North America
ex: Many Western countries have cold winters.

senses.def: covered with or full of water or another liquid
ex: My shoes are wet.
Don't sit on the wet grass.

senses.def: with a lot of rain
ex: It was a cold, wet day.

senses.def: a very large sea mammal that breathes air
ex: We saw a whale from the boat.
Whales sing to each other under the water.

senses.def: used to ask about a thing or a choice
ex: What colour is your car?
What time is it?

senses.def: used to ask for information about something
ex: What is your name?
What do you want to eat?

senses.def: the thing or things that
ex: I don't understand what you said.

mistake.wrong: What you are doing?
mistake.right: What are you doing?
mistake.note: In questions, put the auxiliary verb before the subject.

senses.def: any or every; it does not matter which
ex: Take whatever books you like.
Whatever time you arrive, call me.

senses.def: anything or everything; it does not matter what
ex: You can do whatever you want.
Whatever happens, we will stay together.

senses.def: a cereal plant whose grain is made into flour
ex: The farmers grow wheat and barley.
Bread is made from wheat flour.

senses.def: to breathe with a whistling sound because of difficulty in breathing
ex: He wheezed as he climbed the stairs.

senses.def: used to ask at what time something happens
ex: When does the film start?
When is your birthday?

senses.def: at the time that something happens
ex: I was reading when the phone rang.
Call me when you arrive.

mistake.wrong: When I will arrive, I will call you.
mistake.right: When I arrive, I will call you.
mistake.note: After when, use a present tense for future meaning, not will.

senses.def: used to say that you do not know exactly when something will happen
ex: Come on Friday, or whenever suits you best.

senses.def: every time that; at any time that
ex: Whenever it rains, the road floods.
You can call me whenever you like.

senses.def: used to ask about the place of something
ex: Where do you live?
Where are my keys?

senses.def: in or to the place that
ex: This is the town where I was born.
Put it where you can see it.

senses.def: used to compare two things and show a difference between them
ex: Some people love cities, whereas others prefer the countryside.
He is tall, whereas his brother is short.

senses.def: in or to any place; it does not matter where
ex: Sit wherever you like.
Wherever I go, I take my camera.

senses.def: used to talk about two or more possibilities
ex: I don't know whether he will come.
She asked whether the shop was open.

mistake.wrong: I don't know whether or not to go or not.
mistake.right: I don't know whether to go or not.
mistake.note: Do not repeat 'or not' twice; use whether ... or not once.

senses.def: used to ask about a choice among a limited number of things
ex: Which bus goes to the airport?
Which colour do you prefer?

senses.def: used to ask someone to choose from a group
ex: Which is your bag?
Which do you want, tea or coffee?

senses.def: used to give more information about a thing already mentioned
ex: The book, which I bought yesterday, is great.

senses.def: any one of a number of things; it does not matter which
ex: Take whichever seat you like.

senses.def: any one that you choose
ex: You can have whichever you prefer.

senses.def: during the time that something else is happening
ex: She listened to music while she cooked.
Don't talk while I'm speaking.

senses.def: used to show a contrast between two things
ex: He likes tea, while his wife prefers coffee.

senses.def: a period of time
ex: I haven't seen her for a while.
Wait here for a little while.

senses.def: while; more formal in British English
ex: Whilst I understand your concern, I cannot change the rule.
He read the report whilst waiting.

senses.def: to hit a person or animal with a long thin piece of leather
ex: The rider whipped the horse.

senses.def: to mix cream or eggs quickly until they become thick
ex: Whip the cream until it is stiff.

senses.def: to make a continuous low sound like something spinning quickly
ex: The fan whirred quietly all night.

senses.def: a very strong wind that spins round and round
ex: A whirlwind swept across the field.

senses.def: a situation in which things happen very quickly
ex: They had a whirlwind romance and married in a month.

senses.def: a strong alcoholic drink made from grain, especially in Ireland or the US
ex: He poured a glass of whiskey.

senses.def: a very quiet way of speaking, using your breath rather than your voice
ex: She spoke in a whisper.
I heard a whisper behind me.

senses.def: to speak very quietly so that only one person can hear
ex: She whispered something in his ear.
Don't whisper – it's rude.

senses.def: a small tube that makes a high sound when you blow through it
ex: The referee blew his whistle.
The coach carries a whistle.

senses.def: a high sound made by blowing air through your lips
ex: He gave a long whistle of surprise.

senses.def: to make a high sound by blowing air through your lips
ex: He whistled a happy tune.
The kettle whistled on the stove.

senses.def: having the colour of snow or milk
ex: She wore a white dress.
The walls are painted white.

senses.def: the colour of snow or milk
ex: The room is decorated in white.
Add the white of the egg.

senses.def: used to ask which person or people
ex: Who is that man?
Who called you?

senses.def: used to say which person you are talking about
ex: The woman who lives next door is a nurse.

senses.def: any person; it does not matter who
ex: Whoever finishes first gets a prize.
Give it to whoever wants it.

senses.def: all of something; every part of it
ex: I ate the whole cake.
It rained the whole day.

senses.def: a complete thing made of parts
ex: The whole is greater than the sum of its parts.
On the whole, I enjoyed the trip.

senses.def: completely; in every way
ex: The accident was wholly his fault.
I am not wholly convinced.

senses.def: the object form of 'who', used in formal writing for a person
ex: To whom should I send the letter?
The woman whom I met was very kind.

senses.def: used to ask the reason for something
ex: Why are you late?
I don't know why he left.

mistake.wrong: Why you are crying?
mistake.right: Why are you crying?
mistake.note: In direct questions, put the auxiliary verb before the subject.

senses.def: morally bad or cruel
ex: The wicked queen poisoned the princess.
It was a wicked thing to do.

senses.def: very good or excellent (informal, British)
ex: That was a wicked concert!

senses.def: measuring a large distance from side to side
ex: The river is very wide here.
The road is ten metres wide.

senses.def: including many different things
ex: The shop sells a wide range of books.

senses.def: as far or as much as possible
ex: Open your mouth wide.
The door was wide open.

senses.def: a woman whose husband has died and who has not married again
ex: The widow lives alone in a small house.
He left his money to his widow.

senses.def: the woman that a man is married to
ex: His wife is a doctor.
I'd like you to meet my wife.

senses.def: living or growing in nature, not looked after by people
ex: Wild horses run across the plains.
We picked wild flowers.

senses.def: very excited or not controlled
ex: The crowd went wild when he scored.

senses.def: a large area of land that has not been cultivated or built on
ex: They camped in the wilderness for a week.
The mountains are a protected wilderness.

senses.def: animals and plants that live in nature
ex: The park is full of wildlife.
We must protect wildlife.

senses.def: used to talk about things that are going to happen in the future
ex: It will rain tomorrow.
I'll call you tonight.

senses.def: used to offer, promise or decide to do something
ex: I'll carry your bag.
We will help you.

senses.def: the power of the mind to choose and keep trying to do something
ex: She has a strong will.
He did it against his will.

senses.def: a legal document saying who will receive your things when you die
ex: He left the house to his son in his will.

mistake.wrong: If it will rain, we will stay home.
mistake.right: If it rains, we will stay home.
mistake.note: Do not use will after if in conditional clauses; use the present simple.

senses.def: ready and happy to do something if asked
ex: Are you willing to work at weekends?
She is willing to help.

senses.def: in a way that shows you are happy to do something
ex: He willingly gave up his seat.
I'll willingly help you move house.

senses.def: to be the best or first in a competition, game or fight
ex: Our team won the match.
She won first prize.

senses.def: to get something because of your effort or skill
ex: He won the respect of his colleagues.

senses.def: a victory in a game or competition
ex: It was their third win in a row.

senses.def: with many bends and turns
ex: We drove along a winding road up the mountain.
A winding path led to the beach.

senses.def: the large window at the front of a vehicle (US)
ex: Rain covered the windshield.
A stone cracked the windshield.

senses.def: an alcoholic drink made from grapes
ex: They ordered a bottle of red wine.
Wine is made from grapes.

senses.def: one of the parts of a bird, insect or plane used for flying
ex: The bird spread its wings.
The plane's left wing was damaged.

senses.def: a part of a large building that sticks out from the main part
ex: The hospital has a new east wing.

senses.def: a quick closing and opening of one eye as a friendly signal
ex: He gave me a wink across the room.

senses.def: a person or team that wins a competition
ex: The winner received a gold medal.
Who was the winner of the race?

senses.def: to clean or dry something by rubbing it with a cloth or your hand
ex: She wiped the table with a cloth.
He wiped his hands on a towel.

senses.def: to remove something by rubbing
ex: Wipe the dirt off your shoes.

senses.def: a long thin piece of metal, often used to carry electricity
ex: The fence is made of wire.
Don't touch the bare wire.

senses.def: to connect equipment to an electricity supply with wires
ex: The electrician wired the new lights.

senses.def: having or showing good judgment and experience
ex: She is a wise old woman.
It was wise to leave early.

senses.def: a feeling that you want something to happen
ex: Make a wish and blow out the candles.
His wish came true.

senses.def: good wishes: kind words that you say to someone
ex: Best wishes for the new year!

senses.def: to want something that is not possible or not likely
ex: I wish I had a bigger house.
She wished she could stay longer.

senses.def: to hope that someone will have good luck or happiness
ex: We wish you a happy birthday.

mistake.wrong: I wish I will pass the exam.
mistake.right: I hope I will pass the exam.
mistake.note: Use hope (not wish) for something possible in the future; wish is for unreal situations.

senses.def: sad and thoughtful because you want something that you cannot have
ex: She gave a wistful smile as she looked at the old photos.
He sounded wistful when he spoke of his childhood.

senses.def: the ability to say clever and funny things
ex: He is famous for his quick wit.
Her speech was full of wit.

senses.def: wits: the ability to think quickly and clearly
ex: She used her wits to escape.

senses.def: together or in the company of someone or something
ex: I live with my parents.
Come with me.

senses.def: using something
ex: Cut the bread with a knife.
She wrote it with a pen.

senses.def: having or carrying something
ex: He is a man with a beard.
A girl with a red bag stood nearby.

mistake.wrong: I travelled with the bus.
mistake.right: I travelled by bus.
mistake.note: Use 'by' for means of transport; 'with' is for companions and tools.

senses.def: to take money out of a bank account
ex: I withdrew fifty pounds from the cash machine.

senses.def: to take something back or away
ex: The soldiers withdrew from the town.
She withdrew her complaint.

senses.def: the act of taking money out of a bank account
ex: You can make a cash withdrawal at any branch.

senses.def: the act of leaving a place, activity or agreement
ex: The withdrawal of troops began on Monday.

senses.def: quiet, not wanting to talk to other people
ex: After the accident, he became withdrawn.
The child was pale and withdrawn.

senses.def: before a period of time has finished
ex: I'll finish the work within an hour.
The doctor will see you within a week.

senses.def: inside a place, area or limit
ex: The hotel is within walking distance of the beach.

senses.def: not having or using something
ex: I can't live without music.
She left without her coat.

senses.def: used before -ing to show something is not done
ex: He left without saying goodbye.

senses.def: to see something happen, especially an accident or crime
ex: Many people witnessed the accident.

senses.def: a person who sees an event, especially a crime
ex: The police are looking for witnesses.
She was a witness at the trial.

senses.def: using words in a clever and funny way
ex: He gave a witty speech.
She is a witty writer.

senses.def: excellent (old-fashioned, British informal)
ex: That's a wizard idea!

senses.def: a wild animal like a large dog that lives and hunts in groups
ex: We heard a wolf howling in the forest.
Wolves hunt in packs.

senses.def: an adult female person
ex: A woman was waiting at the door.
She is a very kind woman.

mistake.wrong: Two womans came in.
mistake.right: Two women came in.
mistake.note: The plural of woman is women, with a different vowel sound in the first syllable.

senses.def: to think about something and want to know more about it
ex: I wonder what time it is.
She wondered why he was late.

senses.def: a feeling of surprise and admiration
ex: The children looked at the snow in wonder.

senses.def: something that is amazing
ex: The pyramids are one of the wonders of the world.

senses.def: causing wonder; amazing and beautiful (literary)
ex: They saw wondrous sights on the journey.
A wondrous light filled the sky.

senses.def: to try to win the support or business of someone
ex: The company is trying to woo new customers.

senses.def: to try to win the love of someone (old use)
ex: He wooed her with flowers and poems.

senses.def: the hard material that trees are made of, used for building and burning
ex: The table is made of wood.
They collected wood for the fire.

senses.def: woods: a small forest
ex: We went for a walk in the woods.

senses.def: a single unit of language with a meaning
ex: What does this word mean?
I don't know the English word for it.

senses.def: a short talk or conversation
ex: Can I have a word with you?

senses.def: a job or the place where you do your job
ex: I go to work by bus.
She is looking for work.

senses.def: things that you do using effort to achieve something
ex: I have a lot of work to do today.

senses.def: to do a job, usually to earn money
ex: My father works in a bank.
She works hard.

senses.def: to operate correctly
ex: The washing machine doesn't work.

mistake.wrong: I have many works to do.
mistake.right: I have a lot of work to do.
mistake.note: Work meaning jobs or tasks is uncountable, so it has no plural.

senses.def: having a job, or relating to work
ex: She is a working mother.
Long working hours make him tired.

senses.def: a period of physical exercise to keep fit
ex: I do a workout at the gym every morning.
The workout lasted an hour.

senses.def: a meeting where people learn practical skills or discuss a subject
ex: I attended a writing workshop.
The workshop is for teachers.

senses.def: a room or building where things are made or repaired
ex: He repairs bicycles in his workshop.

senses.def: the planet Earth and all the people and places on it
ex: She has travelled all over the world.
English is spoken all around the world.

senses.def: a particular area of activity or society
ex: He works in the world of fashion.

senses.def: relating to ordinary life and material things, not spiritual matters
ex: He gave away all his worldly goods.
The monks lived without worldly pleasures.

senses.def: having a lot of experience of life
ex: She was a worldly woman who had travelled widely.

senses.def: a long thin creature with no legs that lives in the soil
ex: The bird pulled a worm out of the ground.
Worms live in the earth.

senses.def: damaged or thin because of long use
ex: The carpet is old and worn.
He put on a pair of worn shoes.

senses.def: unhappy because you keep thinking about problems or bad things that might happen
ex: I'm worried about my exam.
She looked worried.

mistake.wrong: I am worried for my exam.
mistake.right: I am worried about my exam.
mistake.note: Use worried about, not 'for', for the thing that causes your worry.

senses.def: a feeling of fear or concern about something
ex: Money is a big worry for them.
He has no worries.

senses.def: to think about problems or bad things that might happen and feel unhappy
ex: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
She worries about her son.

senses.def: to make someone feel anxious
ex: His silence worries me.

senses.def: making you feel anxious
ex: The news about the flood is worrying.
It is worrying that nobody has called.

senses.def: of a lower quality or standard than something else
ex: The weather is worse today.
My English is worse than hers.

senses.def: in a less good or less successful way
ex: He plays worse than he did last year.

senses.def: something that is worse
ex: Worse was to come.

senses.def: the act of showing respect and love for God or a god, such as by prayer
ex: Many people go to a place of worship each week.
The hall is used for worship on Fridays.

senses.def: the lowest in quality or the most bad
ex: This is the worst film I've ever seen.
It was the worst storm in years.

senses.def: the most bad or unpleasant thing
ex: Prepare for the worst.
The worst is over.

senses.def: in the least good way
ex: The south was worst affected by the floods.

senses.def: having a particular value, especially in money
ex: The ring is worth a lot of money.
How much is the house worth?

senses.def: good or important enough to do something
ex: The film is worth seeing.
It's worth asking for help.

mistake.wrong: This book is worth to read.
mistake.right: This book is worth reading.
mistake.note: Worth is followed by an -ing form, not a to-infinitive.

senses.def: having no value or use
ex: The old coins turned out to be worthless.
He felt worthless after losing his job.

senses.def: important or good enough to deserve the time or effort spent
ex: The long trip was worthwhile.
She did a worthwhile job.

senses.def: deserving respect, support or attention
ex: He is a worthy winner.
The cause is worthy of our support.

senses.def: used to make polite requests or offers
ex: Would you like some tea?
Would you open the window, please?

senses.def: used to talk about imagined situations or the future in the past
ex: If I had money, I would buy a car.
He said he would come.

mistake.wrong: If I would have time, I would help you.
mistake.right: If I had time, I would help you.
mistake.note: Do not use would in the if-clause of a conditional.

senses.def: an injury to the body, especially a cut made by a weapon
ex: The nurse cleaned the wound.
He died from a knife wound.

senses.def: to injure someone with a weapon
ex: Three soldiers were wounded in the attack.
His words wounded her deeply.

senses.def: a flat soft bread rolled around food
ex: I had a chicken wrap for lunch.

senses.def: to cover something completely in paper, cloth or other material
ex: She wrapped the present in blue paper.
He wrapped a scarf around his neck.

senses.def: a ship, car or plane that has been badly damaged or destroyed
ex: Divers explored the wreck of the old ship.
The car was a total wreck after the crash.

senses.def: to pull or twist something violently
ex: He wrenched the door open.
She wrenched her arm free.

senses.def: to injure a part of the body by twisting it
ex: I wrenched my shoulder in the fall.

senses.def: the joint between the hand and the arm
ex: She wears a gold watch on her wrist.
He broke his wrist playing football.

senses.def: the activity of putting words on paper or a screen
ex: Writing is my favourite part of the lesson.
Please put your complaint in writing.

senses.def: the way a person forms letters by hand
ex: I can't read your writing.

senses.def: expressed in writing, not spoken
ex: You need written permission from your parents.
The written exam lasts two hours.

senses.def: not correct or not true
ex: You have the wrong number.
Your answer is wrong.

senses.def: not morally right or not acceptable
ex: It is wrong to steal.
What's wrong with you?

senses.def: in a way that is not correct
ex: I spelt your name wrong.
Everything went wrong yesterday.

senses.def: in a way that is not correct, fair or true
ex: He was wrongly accused of stealing.
The letter was wrongly addressed.
